sentences: Revolving credit utilization is the most important driver of predicted default, accounting for about 28% of the model's importance, and risk generally rises as utilization climbs, with the sharpest increases at the high end.
The number of past delinquencies is the second most important driver, and risk increases with it, with most of the rise occurring between zero and one or two delinquencies.
The two features interact strongly: the added risk from high utilization is much larger for applicants with past delinquencies, so the effect of utilization grows with the number of delinquencies.
Income and length of credit history each have a moderate effect, with higher income and longer histories associated with lower predicted risk.
Debt-to-income ratio has a weak effect, and the data do not settle how strongly the remaining features matter beyond the ones named above.
The data do not settle whether number of dependents has any effect, and age and months at the current address show no effect that the data can detect.
Credit history length and recent inquiries interact, with the effect of inquiries reversing direction depending on how long the credit history is.
Utilization does not interact with months at the current address in any practically meaningful way.
